package_info.why_malicious: N/A – This article does not describe a specific malicious package, but rather discusses security challenges and best practices for managing Docker images and binaries to prevent vulnerabilities and malicious artifacts from entering production environments.

behavioral_signatures: Unvetted binaries included in Docker images
Use of cleartext or static credentials for Docker registry access
Lack of fine-grained access control for Docker images and binaries
Absence of automated vulnerability scanning in the CI/CD pipeline
file_indicators: Docker images containing untested or unscanned OS/application packages
Dockerfiles referencing third-party or untrusted sources
network_indicators: Docker registry access over unencrypted channels
Unusual or unauthorized access patterns to Docker registries
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Docker image build and deployment pipelines for inclusion of untested or unscanned binaries. Enforce access controls and audit logs for Docker registry usage. Integrate automated vulnerability scanning (e.g., JFrog Xray) into the CI/CD process to detect and block images with known vulnerabilities. Detect use of cleartext credentials or API keys with no expiration. Review Dockerfiles and image layers for references to untrusted sources.
